title: AngularLynx application builder
description: Builds the Lynx bundle with rspeedy and, with --platform, the iOS and Android binaries.

platform.description: Also build native binaries into dist/<platform>/. Without it, only the bundle is built, as `rspeedy build` does.

run.description: After --platform builds the app, install it on a simulator, emulator or phone and open it. iOS uses the running simulator, or else starts the newest iPhone simulator, and a real iPhone only when --device names it; Android uses the running emulator or connected phone, or else starts the first virtual device.

device.description: With --run, where to open the app: on iOS a simulator's or a paired iPhone's name (e.g. "iPhone 18 Pro", "Jane's iPhone") or UDID, on Android a virtual device's name or an adb serial (e.g. emulator-5554). An iPhone needs ios.teamId.

watch.description: Rebuild the bundle when files change, as Angular's `ng build --watch` does. Can't be combined with `platform`.

config.description: The rspeedy config file, relative to the project root. Defaults to lynx.config.ts (or .js, .mts, .mjs) when the project has one. Without one, the app builds from angular.json: `browser` is the entry, and both the lynx and web environments are built.

environment.description: Only build these rspeedy environments (e.g. lynx). With --platform, only the lynx environment is built.

intl.description: The Intl APIs to add to the Lynx bundle, which Lynx lacks, with data for i18n.sourceLocale and i18n.locales. Needs the FormatJS packages they use installed. The web bundle uses the browser's own.

browser.description: Angular: the app's entry point. Read by @blotch/rsbuild-plugin-angular-lynx and `ng test`, and rspeedy's `source.entry` unless lynx.config.ts sets one.

tsConfig.description: Angular: the tsconfig the app compiles with.

polyfills.description: Angular: modules loaded before the app (e.g. @angular/localize/init).

assets.description: Angular: used by `ng test` only. Lynx bundles reference assets through imports.

inlineStyleLanguage.description: Angular: the language of inline component styles.

fileReplacements.description: Angular: files swapped at build time, e.g. environment files.

aot.description: Angular: ahead-of-time compilation. Defaults to true.

optimization.description: Angular: script and style optimization. Also sets rspeedy's mode: production when scripts are optimized (the default), development otherwise.

outputHashing.description: Angular: hashes in emitted file names.

i18nMissingTranslation.description: Angular: how to report missing translations.

budgets.description: Angular: size budgets, checked against the Lynx bundles (each entry's bundle is its own `initial` budget) and component stylesheets.

extractLicenses.description: Angular: accepted for compatibility with `ng new`.

outputPath.description: Angular: the output folder. Defaults to rspeedy's dist/.

baseHref.description: Angular: the URL path the app is served under, e.g. /shop/. The web bundle's images are requested under it (rspeedy's output.assetPrefix for the web environment), since Lynx for Web resolves them against the page that shows the bundle. The Lynx bundle resolves them against itself and doesn't need it.

index.description: Angular: accepted for compatibility; Lynx apps have no index.html.

appName.description: The app's name under its icon. Defaults to the project name.

appId.description: The iOS bundle ID and Android applicationId, e.g. com.example.myapp.

version.description: The user-facing version, e.g. 1.2.0. Defaults to package.json's version.

buildNumber.description: The store build number (CFBundleVersion / versionCode). Must increase with every store upload.

orientation.description: The screen orientations the app supports.

edgeToEdge.description: Whether the page fills the screen, under the status bar and the home indicator, with CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) carrying the insets. false lays the page out inside the safe area, with env() at 0.

icon.description: The app icon: a 1024×1024 PNG without transparency, relative to the project root. iOS uses it as it is; Android gets it at each screen density, round, and as an adaptive icon.

splash.description: The launch screen, from the tap on the app's icon until the app's first screen is ready: an image centered on a color. The runtime's provideSplashScreen() says when it hides.

image.description: A PNG with transparency, relative to the project root, drawn centered. Without one, iOS shows the color alone and Android the launcher icon.

imageWidth.description: The image's width on screen in points and dp, needed with image. Give the PNG at least three times as many pixels. Android shows the image inside a circle 192 dp across, and draws one whose corners reach past it smaller.

backgroundColor.description: The color behind the image, also painted behind the app (#RRGGBB or #RGB). Defaults to white, and on Android, to black in dark mode.

dark.description: The image and the color in dark mode. Each defaults to the light one.

image.description: A PNG with transparency, drawn at the same imageWidth.

permissions.description: Each permission the app uses, with the reason shown to the user.

savePhotos.description: Why the app adds images to the photo library: iOS shows it the first time someone taps Save Image in LynxShare's share sheet. Defaults to "Saves the images you choose to your photo library."

deepLinkSchemes.description: Custom URL schemes that open the app, e.g. ["myapp"].

canOpenURLSchemes.description: Other apps' URL schemes LynxLinking.canOpenURL() can ask about, e.g. ["whatsapp"]. iOS and Android 11+ answer only for the schemes an app declares. http, https, mailto, tel and sms are always there.

shortcuts.description: Things the app does that the phone offers outside it: on iOS through Siri, Spotlight and the Shortcuts app, and on Android in the menu a long press on the app's icon opens. The app hears each one through LynxShortcuts. iOS takes up to 10.

id.description: What the app's code knows the shortcut by, in LynxShortcuts.on(id, handler), e.g. "show-photos". Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter.

title.description: The name the phone lists it under, e.g. "Show photos".

phrases.description: What the person says to Siri. Each one names the app with {appName}, which Siri requires, e.g. ["Show photos in {appName}"]. Defaults to the title, then "in {appName}". iOS only.

route.description: The path the router navigates to when the shortcut runs, e.g. "/photos". Without one, the app stays where it is.

symbol.description: The SF Symbol iOS draws beside it, e.g. "arrow.clockwise". iOS only.

teamId.description: The Apple Developer team ID that signs the app. On its own, it signs the builds --run --device installs on an iPhone, with the Apple ID signed in to Xcode (a free Apple ID's Personal Team works).

export.description: Builds an .ipa signed this way: app-store-connect for App Store Connect and TestFlight, or release-testing (ad hoc) for the iPhones registered to the team. Defaults to app-store-connect once signing is set; without signing, the Apple ID signed in to Xcode signs it.

signing.description: An App Store Connect API key for headless signing. Each field names the environment variable holding the value.
The Google Play upload key. The *Env fields name the environment variables holding the values.

adaptiveIcon.description: The two layers of the adaptive icon Android 8 and later show. Without it, the adaptive icon is `icon`, scaled so the launcher's mask shows all of it.

foreground.description: A 1024×1024 PNG with transparency, relative to the project root. Keep its content inside the middle 66 of its 108 dp (about 626 px of the 1024): the mask crops the rest.

background.description: A hex color of 6 or 3 digits (e.g. #111111), or a 1024×1024 PNG relative to the project root.
